block.title: Why coffee cools fastest at the start
block.body:
Heat leaves the cup in proportion to the **temperature gap** between the coffee and the room.

```rh-diagram
{"version": 1, "diagram": {"kind": "flow", "title": "Where the heat goes", "nodes": [{"id": "a", "label": "Hot coffee", "role": "process"}, {"id": "b", "label": "Gap to the room large?", "role": "decision"}, {"id": "c", "label": "Loses heat fast", "role": "outcome"}, {"id": "d", "label": "Loses heat slowly", "role": "outcome"}], "edges": [{"from": "a", "to": "b"}, {"from": "b", "to": "c", "label": "Yes"}, {"from": "b", "to": "d", "label": "No"}]}}
```

Just after you pour, the gap is large, so the coffee loses heat quickly.

```rh-illustration
{"version": 1, "id": "steam", "prompt": "A steaming mug of coffee on a wooden table beside a thermometer, flat textbook illustration, no text", "alt": "A steaming mug of coffee beside a thermometer", "caption": "Steam carries heat away fastest while the coffee is hottest."}
```

As it cools the gap shrinks, so the cooling curve flattens near room temperature.
